newsitem.title: INDIA: India's VSNL up 6.6 pct on Bombay bourse.
newsitem.headline: India's VSNL up 6.6 pct on Bombay bourse.

text.p: Shares of India's overseas telecommunications monopoly Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) rose 64.75 rupees, or 6.6 percent, to 1,050 in low volumes on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, traders said.
They said there were some buyers in the local shares after the firm's issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs) was oversubscribed on Monday.
"Speculators are hoping that some investors who didn't get GDR allotments could pick up the local share," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
BSE volumes were low at just 500 shares in early trade.
VSNL said on Monday its GDR issue had been priced at $13.93 per GDR, or 1,000 rupees per VSNL share. It said in a statement the issue had been oversubscribed about 10 times.
The price represented a 1.5 percent premium to VSNL's closing price of March 21. Each GDR represents half an ordinary VSNL share.
